_comment: Firebase web config. These values are NOT secrets — they identify the project, they do not authorise anything. Security comes from firestore.rules and from the authorised-domains list in the Firebase console. Google documents this explicitly. Fill these in from Firebase console → Project settings → Your apps → Web app.
_setup: See docs/SETUP-FIREBASE.md for the full walkthrough.
_moderatorUids: After your first sign-in, put your own uid here so you can moderate. Find it in Firebase console → Authentication → Users. This list only decides which buttons are SHOWN. The actual authority lives in Firestore: the rules require users/<uid>.role == 'moderator', and nobody can grant themselves that field — set it once in the console. A uid listed here without that role sees the buttons and gets a 403, which is the safe direction to be wrong in.
_sdkVersion: Copy the version from the snippet Firebase shows you when you register the web app. If sign-in silently does nothing, this is the first thing to check.
_authProvider: Email/password. Firebase hashes and stores the password; this codebase never sees it. Posting additionally requires a verified email address — see firestore.rules.
